 Shelter-in-place lifted after chemical plant explosion in Mississippi Delta; fire contained 
 By Hannah Kozlowski Published : Nov. 4, 2026 at 10:28 AM CST Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google GREENVILLE, Miss. (WMC) - A shelter-in-place order has been lifted after emergency crews contained a fire sparked by a chemical plant explosion in Washington County Wednesday morning.
 Shelter-in-place issued following chemical plant explosion in Greenville (Washington Co., MS Emergency Operations Center) According to the Washington County Emergency Operations Center (EOC), the fire is now under control. Firefighters and emergency personnel on scene are undergoing decontamination protocols as a precautionary safety measure due to potential chemical exposure. Officials confirmed no injuries have been reported.
 The incident began just after 7 a.m. at the Loveland facility, formerly known as Platte Chemical, located in Greenville. City officials said the initial blast involved a chemical herbicide stored inside a “hot box.”
 Shelter-in-place lifted after chemical plant explosion in Mississippi Delta; fire contained (Washington Co., MS Emergency Operations Center) Multiple agencies responded to battle the blaze, including the Greenville, Riverside, Leland, and Greenville Airport fire departments. Regional HAZMAT teams from surrounding counties, along with representatives from the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and the Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality (MDEQ), were dispatched to assist with containment, air monitoring, and safety operations.
 As thick smoke spread from the facility Wednesday morning, emergency officials issued a shelter-in-place order just before 9:30 a.m. for residents bordered by Highway 182 from Beauchamp to Kuehn Road and VFW from Beauchamp to Kuehn Road. While that order has since been canceled, officials continue to ask the public to steer clear of the immediate facility area while crews wrap up operations.
 Anyone who was in the area and suspects they may have been exposed to hazardous fumes should seek medical evaluation. Symptoms of chemical herbicide exposure can include:
 Burning or watering eyes 
 Persistent coughing or throat irritation 
 Dizziness or severe headaches 
 Nausea or vomiting 
 Chest tightness or shortness of breath 
 Shelter-in-place lifted after chemical plant explosion in Mississippi Delta; fire contained (Washington Co., MS Emergency Operations Center) Greenville Mayor Errick Simmons praised the swift coordination of local and state responders:
 “Our first priority is the safety of our residents, our first responders, and everyone working at or near the facility. We are coordinating with emergency response agencies to assess the situation, contain the fire, and determine whether additional protective measures are necessary,” Mayor Simmons said. “I ask our citizens to remain calm, avoid the immediate area, and allow our firefighters and emergency personnel the space they need to do their jobs safely and effectively. We will continue monitoring this situation closely and providing updates as verified information becomes available. The safety of our people will always come first.”
 Investigations into the exact cause of the explosion remain ongoing.
 This is a developing story. Stay with us online and on-air for updates as more information is confirmed.
